headline: Compact of the Thirteen Tribes Ratified in Underworld Summit
body:
In a summit held forty meters below The Narrows in the cavern network known as the Cradle, representatives of thirteen distinct Bore Rat tunnel communities ratified a mutual governance document today — the Compact of the Thirteen Tribes — establishing the first formal political structure the underground communities have ever claimed. The signing was confirmed by three independent sources with access to the Underworld, though no corponation or Federal Remnant authority has acknowledged the event. The Compact establishes shared tunnel rights, a dispute arbitration council, collective defense obligations, and crucially, a unified tolling structure for surface-dwellers seeking underground passage.

The Thirteen Tribes span communities from the deep thermal tunnels beneath Geartown to the partially flooded passages of Old Harbor's subsurface network. They are not a monolith — the signing reportedly required fourteen months of negotiation and nearly collapsed twice over competing claims to a critical junction called the Crossbone, where four tunnel lines converge beneath the Gray Zone. 'We don't have land,' said one tribal elder who asked to be identified only as Mother Graves. 'We have passage. The Compact is us saying: passage has rules now, and we make them.'

Surface factions are paying attention. The Collective issued a congratulatory statement within hours of the news reaching their mesh network. Iron Lotus has said nothing publicly, though the syndicate is believed to have had embedded operatives at the summit as observers — their existing arrangements with individual Bore Rat communities are now subject to renegotiation under a single unified council rather than tribe by tribe. Axiom Security's Underworld Division, which has spent years attempting to map tunnel access points, faces a significantly more organized adversary.
aftermath: Iron Lotus spent the following year in tense renegotiation with the Compact's newly formed Toll Council, ultimately agreeing to a standardized passage fee structure that cost the syndicate an estimated 30% more annually than its previous patchwork of individual tribal arrangements — but granted it guaranteed access to all thirteen tunnel territories.
runner_relevance: The Compact fundamentally restructured underground runner logistics. Previously, runners could negotiate passage with individual tribal contacts — now all Underworld transit required Compact-sanctioned tolls paid to the unified Toll Council, adding a predictable but unavoidable cost to every tunnel-route contract. Runners with existing tribal relationships became highly valuable as cultural brokers who could navigate the new bureaucracy. Counter-intuitively, the Compact also created new contract types: corponations began hiring runners to gather intelligence on the Compact's internal politics, and Iron Lotus put out work to runners willing to quietly undermine specific tribal representatives ahead of key Toll Council votes.
